requirements.text: Enable law enforcement agencies to capture defendant and incident information along with supporting paper documents within 48 hours of arrest.
Enable magistrates to electronically review request(s) for counsel and submit request(s) for counsel within 24 hours of the indigency hearing.

Enable the Office of Attorney Appointments to review request(s) for counsel and process request(s) for counsel as soon as possible, but not later than the end of the first working day after the date on which the Office of Attorney Appointments receives the request for appointment of counsel.
Enable law enforcement agencies to be notified that the request for counsel has been denied within 24 hours of the denial.
Enable the appointed attorney and Defendant to be notified that an appointment has been made within 24 hours of the appointment.
Enable an appointed attorney to review appointments and capture the date and type of first contact with the defendant no later than the end of the first working day after the date of the appointment.
Enable an appointed attorney to capture the date and time of the first in person visit with the defendant, as appropriate.
Enable the Office of Attorney Appointments to be notified when first contact by an appointed attorney is not made by the of the first working day after the date of the appointment.
Enable the appointed attorney and Office of Attorney Appointments to be notified that the District Attorney has accepted/rejected the incident and whether charges where added, removed or modified.
Enable the Office of Attorney Appointments to produce comprehensive reporting measurements that reflect compliance with the Texas Fair Defense Act.
Implement role-based access control (RBAC) and multi-factor authentication for all users accessing the system, ensuring that access is restricted based on the principle of least privilege.

All sensitive defendant and financial information must be encrypted using industry-standard protocols (e.g., AES-256 for data at rest and TLS 1.2+ for data in transit) to ensure confidentiality and integrity.

The system shall maintain an immutable audit log of all user actions, including record creation, modification, and access, with logs retained for a minimum of seven years to comply with legal record-keeping requirements.
Replace 'as soon as possible' with a specific system latency requirement, such as 'The system shall process and route requests within 5 seconds of submission by the Magistrate.'
Add a requirement: 'The system shall maintain 99.9% availability during business hours (8:00 AM - 5:00 PM CST) to ensure continuous processing of indigent defense requests.'

Add a requirement: 'The system shall perform daily incremental backups and maintain a recovery point objective (RPO) of 1 hour and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 4 hours for all case-related data.'
Add a requirement: 'The system shall support at least 500 concurrent users and process up to 1,000 requests for counsel per day without degradation in performance.'
Define maximum response time for report generation, e.g., 'All reports must be generated within 30 seconds for a 1-year data range.'
Include expected peak concurrent users and daily transaction volume (e.g., 'System must support 50 concurrent users and 500 new appointment requests per day').
Define latency requirements for inter-system data synchronization, e.g., 'Data updates from the Court Case Management System must be reflected in the IJIS within 5 seconds.'
